subject.title: feat: contextual group activation — LLM-driven peeking/engaged state machine

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor LLM-driven contextual activation for group chats, and should that behavior live in shared core activation or behind a plugin/channel API seam?
rationale: Automation can verify the missing mode, but cannot choose the privacy boundary, provider exposure, logging/retention contract, config shape, or long-term owner for processing unmentioned group traffic.

options.title: Sponsor a default-off design first
options.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design covering explicit consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and tests before accepting code.

options.title: Narrow to attention/context primitives
options.body: Keep this broad request open but prioritize lower-risk attention-window, context-window, or passive observation primitives that do not introduce an always-peeking model decision loop.

options.title: Defer to plugin/API groundwork
options.body: Do not add core contextual activation until a trusted observation/decision hook or plugin permission model can safely support it outside core.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a default-off design first
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design covering explicit consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and tests before accepting code.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest history across group activation, channel policy, and current group-gating paths, and the blocker is a cross-cutting product/security choice.
